name: DreamZero
summary: DreamZero takes a 14B video diffusion backbone (Wan 2.1-I2V-14B-480P) and turns it into a joint world-action model, denoising video tokens and action tokens together inside a single monolithic DiT rather than generating a visual plan and inverting it afterwards. Because the same weights that predict pixels also predict actions, the model inherits the internet-scale physical priors of video pretraining, and can be supervised by action-free video. It reports 39.5% average task progress on unseen tasks and a 42% relative gain in cross-embodiment transfer from video-only demonstrations, and it runs closed-loop at 7 Hz — a 38x system-level speedup on Blackwell GB200 that is what makes a 14B diffusion model usable as a controller at all. It scored 1750 Elo on the April 2026 RoboArena leaderboard.
innovation: One objective, one backbone: joint video-and-action denoising in a single DiT, rather than a world model bolted onto a separate action head.
Action-free video becomes first-class training data, so cross-embodiment transfer needs no teleoperation on the target robot.
38x inference optimization turning a 14B video diffusion model into a 7 Hz real-time controller.
matters: The clearest evidence that generative world modelling can replace the VLA recipe outright instead of supplementing it — NVIDIA productized the architecture as GR00T N2 and began marketing 'WAM' as a category.
limits: 7 Hz is real-time only for slow manipulation; contact-rich or dynamic tasks want an order of magnitude more.
Inference cost is far above a comparable VLA, and the reported speedup assumes current NVIDIA silicon.
lineage: UniPi's generate-video-then-act idea collapsed into a single model, on a Cosmos-era video foundation backbone.
